rationale: A permissive project that incorporates strong-copyleft code becomes a derivative work that must be distributed under the GPL, which conflicts with keeping the permissive license (Apache page: GPLv3 software cannot be included in Apache projects).
verification_note: Apache page: "GPLv3 software cannot be included in Apache projects." and "the Apache software would have to be distributed under GPLv3." FSF post: "the terms and conditions of the GNU General Public License cover the whole combination." Scope: Apache page speaks of Apache-licensed projects; we extend it to all permissive licenses.

rationale: Linking statically or dynamically with a GPL module makes a combined work based on it (FSF post), which must then be distributed under the GPL; this is incompatible with a proprietary license.
verification_note: FSF post: "Linking [some program] ABC statically or dynamically with other modules is making a combined work based on ABC." and the GPL "cover[s] the whole combination." Apache page: "would have to be distributed under GPLv3." No source mentions proprietary software; incompatibility follows by inference.

rationale: Design decision by analogy with R2 (AGPL is a GPL-family license). Verified 2026-11-14: no source read states the combined-work consequences for AGPL. verification_note: None of the pages says what happens when AGPL code is combined with proprietary code (FSF post: AGPL NOT STATED; Kemitchell: proprietary NOT STATED). Kemitchell supports only that section 13 needs modification plus remote network interaction. Demoted to design decision.

rationale: Design decision by analogy with R1 (AGPL is a GPL-family license). Verified 2026-11-14: no source read states the combined-work consequences for AGPL.

rationale: Allowed under conditions: with dynamic linking the application source may stay proprietary, with static linking it may not (Qt LGPL page); MPL copyleft is file-level and new files are not Modifications (MPL FAQ Q11). The library stays under its own license, and its source and license text must be provided.
verification_note: Qt page: "In case of dynamic linking, it is possible, but not mandatory, to keep application source code proprietary"; static linking: the application "may no longer be work that uses the library"; user must be able to re-link; library source and LGPL text must be provided. MPL FAQ Q11: "new files containing no MPL-licensed code are not Modifications".

rationale: Same conditions as R5: the weak-copyleft component keeps its own license obligations (library source, license text, relinking), the rest of the project can stay permissive.
verification_note: Same quotes as R5 (Qt LGPL page; MPL FAQ Q11, Q12). Sources cover LGPL and MPL; we generalise to the weak-copyleft category.

rationale: A dependency whose license is unknown, non-standard or not recorded cannot be assessed; manual review is required. No published source consulted; this is a conservative design choice.
Permissive licenses impose only notice/attribution conditions, so a permissive project can depend on permissive packages. No published source consulted in this iteration.
Permissive licenses allow use in proprietary products subject to attribution. No published source consulted in this iteration.
Permissively licensed code can be included in GPL projects; example given for Apache 2 into GPLv3. Exception handled at license level: GPL-2.0-only with Apache-2.0 (see incompatibleWith).
verification_note: Apache page: "Apache 2 software can therefore be included in GPLv3 projects". Only Apache-2.0 into GPLv3 is stated; extension to all permissive licenses is our generalisation. GPLv2 is explicitly not compatible with Apache 2 (handled by lg:incompatibleWith).
